messages:
morgan: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — posting a few clarifying Qs for leadership. I'll list them inline, please reply where helpful.

morgan: 1) How would you summarize our mission in a single sentence for a prospect who asks what makes Redwood different?

sam: Our mission line is still: make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team. Emphasize 'serving' not model ownership. We're selling predictable latency, cost controls, and deployment flexibility across hosted/dedicated/private.

morgan: 2) Can you give one short pitch vs hyperscaler managed endpoints?

eli: Short pitch: hyperscalers give managed models; we give a production-grade serving runtime + operational levers that control unit economics (batching, caching, quantization) + rollout/traceability primitives. Put another way: same API surface, but tuned for production cost & latency.

tara: To add — our benchmarks and evals are a key GTM asset. We show customers real token-cost and p95 latency numbers on similar workloads. That often wins over vague performance claims.

morgan: 3) What's the ideal customer profile for the next 12 months? startups vs enterprise?

sam: Primarily AI-native startups and mid-market product teams pushing LLM features to users. Also platform teams inside larger orgs who need standardized inference. Enterprise/private is strategic but higher-touch.

devin: 4) What top metrics should teams track to know if we're winning in the market? (so we can align product/eng priorities)

sam: Short list: ARR expansion in targeted segments, net retention for inference customers, latency SLO attainment (p95 under target), cost per 1M tokens for representative workloads, and sales cycle time for Dedicated/Private deals.

morgan: 5) Competitors: should we call out "build vs buy" or compare directly to X cloud AI products in messaging?

eli: We should lean into "build vs buy" for technical buyers — show the total cost of ownership and time-to-prod delta. Against cloud AI providers, call out our production controls (SLA, routing, autoscale), and against self-hosted runtimes, stress the orchestration + managed fallback policies and observability. Keep comparisons factual and example-driven.

tara: Tactical: we'll produce a one-pager mapping persona -> deployment recommendation (hosted for fast dev, dedicated for scale, private for compliance) and 2 benchmark callouts per persona.

sam: Action items: @tara to draft the persona/deployment cheat sheet, @eli to drop 2 benchmark slides and a short TCO example, @devin to identify one customer success story we can anonymize.

morgan: Thanks — super helpful. Any objections to publishing a short blog/FAQ that covers these FAQ points?

sam: No objections. Do it. Keep it tight, < 800 words, and include one concrete benchmark. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Note: all-hands recording and slides uploaded -> https://redwood.internal/all-hands/3124001234

morgan: Perfect — tagging this thread resolved for follow-ups. Appreciate the quick answers! :raised_hands:
